theory: The statement that a square root has a positive and a negative solution confuses the principal square root with the two solutions of $x^2=a$ for $a>0$; distinguish these and avoid implying two distinct solutions when $a=0$. The procedure also omits the square-root method used by the booklet and candidate, treats every right-hand side as a given constant despite expression equations, and says to solve for $x$ even in coefficient questions; align the procedure with these supported tasks.
